acceptance: compare gains a documented --min-regression-delta option with unit tests for a query that exceeds both limits, one that exceeds only the percentage, one that exceeds only the delta, and the usage error without --fail-on-regression
The nightly-v2 perf step and perf-smoke.yml use the option, and the chosen floor and its derivation from retained artifacts are recorded in the PR description
A large slowdown on a long-running query still fails the gate in a test
docs/development/perf-smoke.md and the compare CLI reference describe the floor
context: Merged as PR #2812 (2026-10-09). Floor is 7 ms, derived in the PR body: compare reads the last recorded execution per query, and the largest per-query spread across the nine retained nightlies on that value is 5.4 ms (Q18), so 1.25 x 5.4 rounds up to 7. The option applies to per-query comparisons only; it is rejected without --fail-on-regression, in platform-run mode and in the wizard's platform branch. The CLI surface guard pins compare's accepted options and help by digest instead of exempting the module. Issue #2778 stays open until the nightly-v2 verification dispatch shows t3:perf passing, and until t3-perf-baseline-refresh-20261008 has also merged.
description: The nightly T3 perf gate and the per-PR Performance Smoke workflow (.github/workflows/perf-smoke.yml) both compare against _project/baselines/perf_smoke_duckdb_tpch_001.json with `--fail-on-regression 10%`, which judges each query by percentage change alone. In nightly run 37794806634 (2026-10-08) total time improved 20.35% and 19 of 22 queries got faster, but Q8 (9.0 to 11.6 ms, +28.9%) and Q20 (10.0 to 11.9 ms, +19.0%) failed on a 2 to 3 ms change. `benchbox compare` has no minimum absolute delta, so it cannot tell scheduling jitter from a regression at this scale. Raising the threshold to 20% is not enough: Q8 would still fail. Add `--min-regression-delta` (a duration such as 5ms or 0.005s, default none so existing callers are unchanged). A per-query comparison then counts as a regression only when it exceeds the percentage threshold and the absolute slowdown exceeds the floor; aggregate metrics stay percentage-only; using the option without --fail-on-regression is a usage error. Use it in the nightly-v2 perf step and perf-smoke.yml. Choose the floor from retained t3-perf-result artifacts: 5 ms unless their per-query run-to-run spread exceeds 4 ms, in which case 1.25 times the largest spread rounded up to whole milliseconds, capped at 15 ms. Update docs/development/perf-smoke.md and the compare CLI reference.
